34. Workshop: prepare a material and UV test

Use a diagnostic texture before the final atlas

Create a small image with unmistakable corner colors and a simple asymmetric mark. Assign it through an Image Texture node connected to Principled Base Color. Set the intended interpolation and unwrap the mesh to the active UV map. Export and compare the four corners in TrickRoom before investing in a detailed atlas.

The material tests explicitly verify top-left red, top-right green, bottom-left blue and a mid-grey corner. They also check that sRGB conversion preserves the expected grey rather than making it unexpectedly dark. This is a useful template for testing a new export setup.

material.use_nodes = True
nodes = material.node_tree.nodes
shader = nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
shader.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = 0.0
shader.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 1.0
texture = nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")
texture.image = atlas_image
texture.interpolation = "Closest"
material.node_tree.links.new(
    texture.outputs["Color"], shader.inputs["Base Color"]
)

Move from test texture to atlas

Replace the diagnostic image with the final atlas without changing the UV convention. Check island padding, seams and mipmap behavior. Avoid attaching a normal/AO/metallic map and assuming the runtime will approximate it. Bake the intended contribution into the base color or choose a deliberately unlit material.

For cutouts, use Blender's supported glTF alpha-mask node recipe and inspect the exported alphaMode and cutoff in the asset report/JSON. The runtime accepts MASK, not layered BLEND. A transparent texel in OPAQUE mode remains opaque by definition.

Confirm normals separately

View a plain material without the atlas to inspect shading and backface behavior. Then restore the texture and inspect UVs. If both are debugged simultaneously, a dark flipped face may look like a texture failure and a stretched texture may look like poor geometry.

Keep an exported material test as part of the asset package while qualifying a new rig or Blender version. It is small, reproducible evidence that the color/UV path works, and it is easier to diagnose than a complex full character.

35. Workshop: final handoff checklist and exact commands

Validate the export copy

Use an explicit Blender executable path and a revisioned source. The following commands are run from the TrickRoom repository root. They do not download a character or open a phone camera.

& $Blender --background Character.blend `
  --python-exit-code 1 `
  --python tools\blender\preflight.py -- `
  --report .local\character-source-report.json

& $Blender --background Character.blend `
  --python-exit-code 1 `
  --python tools\blender\export_character.py -- `
  --output exports\Character-r02.glb

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m trickroom `
  --validate-avatar exports\Character-r02.glb `
  --report .local\character-runtime-report.json

Inspect without conflating modes

Load the model with the synthetic demo. Select bind, then each exported clip, then live. Check both the full stage and the head-detail inset. Use the clean-output window to review what a capture consumer would see, without the configuration panel.

.\Start-TrickRoom.ps1 -Demo `
  -Avatar exports\Character-r02.glb

Render a recorded movement review from the CLI

Before a live-camera session, an explicitly selected recording can drive an unattended model test:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m trickroom `
  --avatar exports\Character-r02.glb `
  --source references\movement.mp4 `
  --render-video .local\character-r02-review.mp4 `
  --snapshot .local\character-r02-last.png `
  --no-mirror

This writes a synthetic MP4 and aggregate JSON, without Studio or raw input/audio. Every selected frame is processed; slow inference does not shorten the output. Add --start-seconds 16 --seconds 3 for a short source interval. Output timing follows reported FPS, not exact VFR timestamps. Existing outputs are protected; use a new name for each revision.

The PNG shows the last rendered frame. Inspect body proportions, articulation, twist, clothing and facial shapes alongside the report's availability counts. Missing observations are not automatically model defects, and a successful export does not certify perfect rigging or appearance. The CLI guide has absolute-path commands for another chat/base.

Only after these steps should you connect the actual IP Webcam feed. Verify automatic framing, rotation/mirroring, and run the movement/facial/crop/loss checklist. Do not store camera URLs or credentials in the exported model, profile, handbook or acceptance report.

Seal the model revision

Check Required evidence
Source preparation Preflight result and source Blender version
Export New GLB, profile and hash receipt
Structure Runtime validation report for the exact GLB
Deformation Bind, clips and combined facial checks
Recorded motion Reference hash, model hash, synthetic MP4 and frame/availability report
Live behavior Actual framing/movement observations, separately labelled
Appearance Explicit artistic feedback, not inferred approval
Reversibility Previous good source/export preserved

The .blend remains the editable source; the GLB/profile pair is the runtime deliverable. Do not overwrite an accepted release with an experiment. Use a new revision name, compare it under the same tests, and record what changed. A model that is easy to trace, validate and revert is far more useful than a beautiful export whose provenance is uncertain.
